title: 5 Myths About Tučepi's Top Attractions, Corrected
metaDescription: Tučepi's real highlights: the long pebble beach, Biokovo Skywalk (€10–15 park ticket), water sports and the old village. Five myths corrected.
content:
## Myth 1: Tučepi is just a beach town with nothing else to see

**The reality:** The beach is the main draw, but it is not the only one. Tučepi has one of the longest beaches on the Makarska Riviera, a pebble shore backed by a shaded promenade, with Biokovo rising directly behind it. The mountain, a nature park since the 1980s, is the reason the village works as a full-week base and not a two-night stop.

**Better approach:** Treat the day in two halves. Swim and use the water-sports operators in the morning, when the pebbles are quieter and the sea is calm. Keep the afternoon or early evening for the mountain. The central beach and the promenade are the best starting point because cafes, rentals and the harbour all sit within a few minutes' walk.

**Insider perspective:** Tučepi is one of the quieter resorts on this stretch of coast, and most accommodation is in private houses and a few established hotels. That is why the beach rarely feels crowded even in August, which cannot be said of Makarska.

## Myth 2: Biokovo Skywalk is a quick stop you can decide on the day

**The reality:** The Skywalk is a horseshoe-shaped glass walkway, about 8.5 m long, that extends roughly 11 m over a cliff edge. It stands at 1,228 m in the Ravna Vlaška area, beside the info centre at the 13th kilometre of the Biokovo road. It is the first skywalk in Croatia and it sits inside Biokovo Nature Park, so there is no separate Skywalk ticket. You buy a park ticket instead.

Current adult park prices:

- **€10** from 1 April to 31 May and in October
- **€15** from 1 June to 30 September
- Children under 7 enter free

Vehicle entry is limited, at about 20 vehicles per full hour, and tickets are sold online with a time slot. The walkway is seasonal and closes in the colder months, so a visit in November or early spring may only give access to the mountain, not the glass platform. Check the park's website before planning.

**Better approach:** Book the ticket and time slot the day before. Aim for the first morning slot or a late afternoon one. Midday in July and August brings the heaviest queues on the platform, and the time on the walkway itself is short, around 30 minutes on most tours. Early visits also give clearer views toward the islands.

**Opinionated take:** Skip the Skywalk at midday in peak summer. You will pay the highest ticket price of the year to stand in a line on a platform that holds only a few people at a time. An early or late slot gives you the same view for the same money without the wait.

## Myth 3: Renting a car and driving up yourself is the cheapest, easiest option

**The reality:** The Biokovo road is the highest road in Croatia and it climbs to the top of Sveti Jure. The stretch to the Skywalk is steep, narrow and full of curves, and in several places only one car fits through. Tučepi to the Skywalk takes about 45 minutes with no stops. Meeting oncoming traffic on a hairpin is the usual problem, and the entry limit means you may wait at the gate if you arrive without a slot.

A guided tour solves most of this. Typical formats from Makarska and the surrounding resorts include:

- Minibus tours of about 2.5–3 hours, from roughly €50
- Land Rover or open jeep tours that continue to Sveti Jure, from roughly €50–70
- Tuk-tuk, buggy and e-bike options at a higher price

Check whether the park entry is included. Some operators sell transport only and collect the €8–15 entry on the bus, in cash. A quoted price of €50 can therefore become €60–65 per person.

**Better approach:** If the driver is comfortable on mountain roads, driving yourself is possible with a booked slot. For everyone else, a jeep tour that includes Sveti Jure (1,762 m, the second-highest peak in Croatia) offers more value than the Skywalk alone, since the platform takes under half an hour and the peak road is the real scenery.

**Insider perspective:** Departures at about 8:00 and 17:00 are common for Makarska Riviera tours. The late departure is usually the better one, as the light softens over the coast and the temperature on the ridge drops by several degrees.

## Myth 4: Hiking up to the Skywalk is an easy walk from the village

**The reality:** The marked loop from Tučepi that passes the Church of St. Catherine on its way to the Skywalk is rated difficult. It runs about 16.6 km with more than 1,200 m of elevation gain and takes close to 8 hours. In July and August the lower slopes have little shade and temperatures at sea level are high.

**Better approach:** Hike only between late April and early June or in late September and October, start before 7:00 and carry at least 2 litres of water per person. For a shorter walk, the Church of St. Catherine, a pre-Ottoman chapel above the village, is a more reasonable target. For heat and time reasons, many visitors take a vehicle up and walk down only a part of the route.

## Myth 5: The old village and the churches are not worth the time

**The reality:** Tučepi's older settlement sits above the coast in Gornje Tučepi. The Parish Church of St. Anthony of Padua, built in a Neo-Romanesque style in 1901, stands there as a reminder of where most residents lived before moving closer to the sea. At the shore, several baroque summer residences from the 18th century, built for noble families, remain from the earlier period. Other chapels in the area include the Church of St. Michael from the 18th century.

**Better approach:** Plan a short evening walk of about 1–2 hours from the harbour toward the upper village. Dress for the heat, carry water and go before sunset. It costs nothing, and it shows a side of the village that the beachfront does not.

## Water sports are the other headline activity

The central beach has operators for parasailing, jet skis, banana boats and boat rental. Prices vary by season and operator and are posted at the stands, so compare two or three before paying. A sunrise or early morning session usually has the calmest sea. Families with young children should note that the pebble shore and clear, gradually deepening water suit supervised swimming, but water shoes help on the stones.

## What to Prioritise in a Three-Day Tučepi Stay

Three things carry the trip: the beach, the Skywalk and Sveti Jure on a guided tour, and one evening in the upper village.

- **Day 1:** Beach and promenade. Try one water-sport session in the morning.
- **Day 2:** Book the Skywalk slot online and take a tour that includes Sveti Jure. Budget €60–75 per person with the park ticket.
- **Day 3:** Walk up to Gornje Tučepi and the Church of St. Anthony of Padua, then return to the sea.

Book the mountain first, as it depends on weather and limited vehicle slots, and fit the beach days around it. If the forecast shows wind or cloud on the ridge, swap the days.

faq.question: But isn't Skywalk Biokovo free to visit?
faq.answer: No. The Skywalk is inside Biokovo Nature Park, and entry requires a park ticket. Adults pay €10 from April to May and in October, and €15 from June to September. Children under 7 enter free. Tickets are sold online with a time slot.

faq.question: Isn't the Skywalk open all year?
faq.answer: No. The glass walkway is seasonal and has been reported closed from November until spring, though the mountain itself remains open. Check the Biokovo Nature Park website for current dates before booking a tour.

faq.question: Isn't it easy to drive up to the Skywalk without a tour?
faq.answer: It is possible, but the road is steep and narrow, with passing only in some sections. About 20 vehicles enter per hour, and the drive takes about 45 minutes from the coast. Many visitors prefer a guided jeep or minibus tour for that reason.

faq.question: Isn't a Skywalk tour price all-inclusive?
faq.answer: Not always. Some tours include the park ticket and others charge €8–15 extra, sometimes in cash on the bus. Confirm what is included when booking.

faq.question: Isn't the Skywalk the highest point you can reach?
faq.answer: No. The Skywalk is at 1,228 m. The highest peak, Sveti Jure, reaches 1,762 m and can be reached by the same Biokovo road, usually on jeep tours that go beyond the platform.

faq.question: But isn't Tučepi too quiet for activities?
faq.answer: It is quieter than Makarska, but it offers water sports on the central beach, hiking above the village and a historic upper settlement. The Skywalk and Biokovo are about 45 minutes away by road.

faq.question: Isn't the hike to the Skywalk suitable for casual walkers?
faq.answer: No. The loop via the Church of St. Catherine is about 16.6 km with over 1,200 m of climbing and takes around 8 hours. It suits fit hikers in spring or autumn, not a hot summer day.

quickAnswer: Tučepi is not a lesser version of Makarska with nothing to do. The long pebble beach, Biokovo Skywalk at 1,228 m, the water sports and the old hillside village make it a complete base. The park ticket costs €10–15, and the Skywalk runs on a seasonal, timed-entry system.
